doc.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013

title: Campus politics: the Buckwheat Zydeco menu
summary: He tells how administrators accused a colleague of racism over a Buckwheat Zydeco menu and urges staying objective.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: so many of these kids coming to the college don’t belong in college. You know? And there’s a lot of support at Buffalo State and this was a very black dominated administration at the high end, when Muriel came in and you had to be very careful what you said. I remember Don Metz, who runs the stuff over at Birchfield, he’s an avante garde player, he’s a fabulous fabulous person, probably the best friend I have here. That’s why I do a lot of stuff with them. And he always cooked a lot of food. Great food. So there’s a guy, Stanley Durell, Buckwheat Zydeco. So he had this thing, this menu, some of this administration was going to come to this, this Buckwheat Zydeco menu. And all of a sudden without checking, the president and three or four of the people wanted diversity, started making phone calls and took him to task for this racist thing he was doing. And I said, “Pardon?” I said, “Do you have any idea who Buckwheat Zydeco is?” Fuckers. You know? They’re so ready to jump. So it’s a dangerous thing with jazz.
And academia, and you have to be very careful and I just try to say let’s stay objective.
